title: The seed with nothing inside
hook: a father has his son break a banyan seed until there's nothing to see, and the smallest verb carries the week
carry: tat tvam asi: the unseen essence is you
tomorrow: a blind king asks one question. which word gives him away?

segments.voice: Yesterday, vasudhaiva kutumbakam: to a wide heart, the earth is family, because one Self lives in all. Today the week comes back, through a seed, and something new begins.

Uddalaka has one more lesson for his son. Bring me a fruit from that banyan tree, he says. Shvetaketu brings it. Break it. What do you see? Tiny seeds, sir. Break one. What do you see? Nothing at all, sir. And the father says: that finest essence you can't see, from it this whole great banyan stands. That finest essence is the self of everything. That is the real. That is the atman. Tat tvam asi.
screen: `BREAK THE FRUIT.` → `BREAK THE SEED.` → `NOTHING AT ALL, SIR.`

segments.voice: That, you are. Three words, and the one doing the heavy lifting is the smallest: asi, you are. It belongs to the smallest verb there is, to be. Asmi, I am, from so 'ham asmi. Asi, you are, from tat tvam asi. Asti, is, hiding inside nasti, is not. Same core, as, with mi for I, si for you, ti for he, she or it. Now run the week back through that seed: a king who burned off his anger in tapas and was called a seer. A warrior told that the atman is never born and never dies. Two schools hearing tat tvam asi as one, or as forever two. A voice behind the sun saying so 'ham asmi. A guest welcomed like God. The earth as one family, because one Self lives in all. Every one of those leans on to be. That's why the next stretch of the path starts a list of two hundred core words, the plain ones these texts keep returning to, with asmi, asi and asti. The biggest claim Hindu scripture makes about who you are rests on the smallest word. And many teachers read it as something to live by: on the days you feel like only your grades, your job or your worst mistake, the Upanishad points underneath, to an essence nobody can see and nothing can break. A seed you can't see holds up a tree.
screen: `ASMI, ASI, ASTI.` · `TAPAS · ATMAN · ONE OR TWO · SO 'HAM · GUEST · ONE FAMILY.` · `TWO HUNDRED PLAIN WORDS.` · then, large: `THE SMALLEST WORDS HOLD THE BIGGEST CLAIMS.`

segments.voice: Say the three forms out loud, slowly, one per breath: asmi, I am; asi, you are; asti, it is. Then, like Shvetaketu, look at something small near you: a seed, a leaf, your own open hand. Let tat tvam asi sit with it, without explaining. Then let the words go, and rest in simply being here.
Two hundred core words: the plain words a reader meets again and again. First up, the verb to be: asmi, asi, asti. The smallest verb, holding up the biggest line.
Here's the line: tat tvam asi, the unseen essence is you. A week well walked.

fork.setup: your little cousin asks what tat tvam asi means, word by word. what do you say?
options: tat, that; tvam, you; asi, are: that unseen essence, you are it.
tat, you; tvam, are; asi, God: it means you are God.
it's one word for 'seed', from the father's story.
fork.reveal: tat, that; tvam, you; asi, are. in the seed story, 'that' is the finest essence nobody can see, from which the banyan stands.

chat.says: draft 1 done!! ending with nani's seed story: 'tat tvam asi.' sam read it and asked: so hindus think they're god??
options: not like that: the father says the unseen essence of everything is what you really are. some schools hear one with God, some hear forever close but two.
yes: it means each person is the creator and can do anything.
no: it's just a line about how trees grow from seeds.
chat.meaning: In Chandogya 6.12, Uddalaka shows Shvetaketu the unseen essence in a banyan seed, the self of everything, and says tat tvam asi: that, you are. Advaita hears the self and Brahman as one; Dvaita hears the soul as forever distinct from God and close to Him.

tie.story: Uddalaka had Shvetaketu break a banyan seed until he saw nothing, then said that unseen essence holds up the tree, and tat tvam asi.
tie.friend: Priya can tell Sam it isn't a boast: Nani's line says the real you is the unseen essence in everything, read as one with God or as forever close.
tie.you: what small thing near you could you look at that way today?
